Backups, printable summaries and reminders (.ics) are generated in your browser and downloaded to your device; they never pass through any server. If you share these files, you decide where they go.
The data lives only in this browser and device. If you clear the browser’s data, it will be lost: that is why a backup is a good idea.

The tools (mood log, thought diary, behavioural activation, sleep diary, panic log and social anxiety tools) and your preferences (dark mode, text size) are stored only in your browser using its local storage (localStorage). Nothing is sent to any server. You can delete them at any time from the tools themselves or by clearing the site data in your browser.

Putting words to what is happening to you is a big step. Here are ideas and phrases to start with family, your GP and at work.
They may ask for a blood test to rule out physical causes (for example thyroid problems or anaemia).
They may propose follow-up, treatment or a referral to a psychologist or a mental health centre (CSMA).
You can bring someone with you. If you don’t feel listened to, you have the right to ask for another appointment or a second opinion.
You can ask for reasonable changes: flexible hours, working from home some days, sharing out tasks, breaks, or reducing a temporary workload. Some example phrases:
You can simply say: “My doctor has signed me off for health reasons”.
You can say: “I haven’t been feeling well for a while and I don’t know what to do. Can you help me?”. That is enough. More ideas in the “How to talk about it” guide.
